summary: Guidance requested: client-side backoff + burst allowance for heavy short-lived job bursts on Dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Acme Retail is observing intermittent 429 responses when submitting short-lived, high-concurrency inference jobs to their Dedicated GPU pool. Traffic pattern: periodic spikes of hundreds of small requests (~50–200 requests within 30–90s) triggered by nightly batch jobs and ad-hoc manual runs. They expected Dedicated to absorb bursts but see throttling and queueing behavior.

Impact:
- Visible failed requests returning 429s for a subset of batch workers causing retries and missed deadlines for downstream grading pipelines.
- Increased end-to-end job latency and operator time spent tuning clients.

Environment:
- Customer: Acme Retail (dedicated tenant)
- Deployment: Dedicated pool, prod/us-east-1
- Models: redwood-v1-13b (primary), gpt-neox-20b-quantized (fallback)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Kick off 100 parallel inference calls (each 1–3 tokens context, <64 tokens output) from 10 worker machines over 60s window.
2) Observe ~15–25% of requests return 429 with X-RateLimit headers present.
3) Repeat with different inter-arrival patterns (burst vs. evenly spaced) — bursts produce more 429s.

Expected behavior:
Dedicated pool should allow configured reserved throughput with transient burst tolerance; client-side retries/backoff should gracefully handle transient 429s without overwhelming scheduler.

Actual behavior:
429s returned quickly for a subset of calls, and retries lead to retry storms. Customer requests guidance on recommended client-side backoff strategies, whether dedicated pool has tunable burst tokens, and how rate-limiter buckets map to per-tenant and per-route quotas.

Logs / headers provided by customer (redacted):
- Example response headers: RateLimit-Limit: 600, RateLimit-Remaining: 0, RateLimit-Reset: 15
- Request ids: r-ff12a3b, r-cd98e4f

Workarounds tried by customer:
- Implemented naive exponential backoff with jitter (base 200ms, max 5s) — still saw occasional failures and increased total job runtime.
- Staggered worker launches — reduced but did not eliminate 429s.

Customer asks:
1) Recommended backoff algorithm and parameters for bursty short jobs on Dedicated pools.
2) Whether there is a per-tenant burst token bucket or only long-term quotas.
3) Guidance on server-side knob(s) we can adjust (rate-limiter windows, burst allowance, scheduler soft-limits) on the Dedicated pool for their contract.
4) If we recommend client changes, sample pseudocode integration and monitoring signals to track.
comments: 2026-03-09 Marcus Chen: Acknowledged. Marcus to triage with infra rate-limiter owners and reach out to SRE. Asked customer for request traces and exact timestamps.

2026-03-09 Aarti Patel: Customer uploaded request traces and header dumps to linked Confluence page. Noted traffic originates from ephemeral job runners; tokenization short so compute per-call is small.

2026-03-10 Sofia Alvarez (SRE): Initial hypothesis — dedicated pool enforces both per-tenant sustained throughput and short-term rate-limiter buckets at the gateway. Need to confirm burst-token policy for Dedicated plan. Assigned to Marcus for config checks.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 Marcus Chen: Checked rate-limiter config for acme-retail dedicated pool. There is a two-layer limiter: per-tenant sustained quota (tokens/min) and gateway per-second bucket with a default burst of 100 tokens. Customer's pattern exceeded gateway burst capacity in <60s windows.
2026-03-11 Marcus Chen: Verified scheduler logs — no GPU saturation. Serving runtime latency per token is nominal. Throttling occurs pre-scheduler at API gateway when concurrent connections spike.

2026-03-11 Sofia Alvarez: Reproduced locally with loadtest script against a staging dedicated pool, saw identical 429 pattern when pushing >120 requests within 30s. Gateway RateLimit-Remaining fell to 0; RateLimit-Reset around 10–20s.

2026-03-12 Marcus Chen: Consulted with product: Dedicated customers can request burst increases and gateway burst window adjustments but changes require ops approval and are global to the pool. Documented options for customer and guidance for safe increases.
resolution: 2026-03-12 Workaround provided to customer: implement capped concurrency at client-side (limit to 80 parallel inflight requests), use jittered exponential backoff (initial 150ms, multiplier 2, max 3s, full-jitter), and add a short pre-flight token-bucket check to avoid hitting gateway hard limits.

2026-03-12 Server-side actions suggested: allow Acme Retail to request a +50% gateway burst allowance for the Dedicated pool during nightly windows; this requires a scheduled ops change and explicit rollback policy. Opened INT-411 to track ops change and safety review.

Follow-up: Marcus to run controlled canary change in staging and provide sample client backoff pseudocode and a monitoring dashboard for RateLimit-Remaining trends. Schedule follow-up call with Acme on 2026-03-15.
